title: Ardent Labs - Discovery: migration OpenAI -> Dedicated
summary: Initial discovery with Ardent Labs focused on migrating from OpenAI hosted endpoints to Redwood Dedicated. Main concerns: latency/cost tradeoffs, eval parity with current models, private VPC options, and security compliance. Agreed next steps include running a short benchmark, sharing security docs and pricing, and scheduling a technical deep dive with infra team.

Jia to schedule technical deep dive / benchmark run (by 2026-03-09)

Priya to provide network constraints and VPC requirements (by 2026-03-06)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jia (Redwood SE), Oliver (Redwood CSM), Maya (Ardent CTO), Liam (Ardent ML Eng), Priya (Ardent Infra), Noah (Product)

[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. Quick intro from our side - I'm Samir, AE, Jia is our SE and will help with the deep dive and benchmarks, Oliver is CSM. How about you folks?
[00:08] Maya (Ardent CTO): Hey, Maya here. Liam, Priya and Noah with me. We're looking at migrating some prod traffic off of OpenAI to either a dedicated Redwood deployment or private. We're mainly concerned about latency, cost, and parity with our current evals.
[00:20] Samir: Great, that's exactly what we'll try to cover. Quick agenda: current stack + constraints, goals for migration, perf/eval parity, security/compliance, and next steps. Sound ok?
[00:27] Maya: Yep.
[00:34] Liam (Ardent ML Eng): I'll add - we use a mix of GPT-like open models on OpenAI but also run vLLM in-house for some latency-sensitive paths, and some TGI-backed endpoints for fine-tuned models. So compatibility with vLLM/TGI workflows is important.
[00:45] Jia (Redwood SE): Good to know. A lot of customers have a hybrid setup similar to that. Can you share rough qps / tokens per month? Means we can size Dedicated appropriately.
[00:55] Noah (Product): Currently around 400 requests per second at peak, average prompt+response ~1,200 tokens, monthly token volume around 1.2B. Latency SLO for our critical path is p95 < 150ms.
[01:10] Samir: Ok, that gives us a baseline. Two quick clarifications: is the 150ms p95 measured end-to-end including network? And are you using streaming today?
[01:18] Priya (Infra): It's measured end-to-end from our app to OpenAI and includes network. We do streaming for some chat flows but not for all endpoints.
[01:26] Jia: Thanks. A few things to call out up front - Redwood Dedicated can give you predictable throughput and lower unit cost, but there are tradeoffs. We often recommend a small pilot to check eval parity because tiny differences in tokenization/kernels can change outputs.
[01:40] Liam: When you say parity, do you mean exact match to OpenAI behavior? We have evaluations that are brittle to small shifts.
[01:47] Jia: Exact match is unlikely - model weights and serving stack differ. But we can get the same quality/utility often within your eval tolerances. Two levers: model variant selection (we carry a catalog of verified open models and optimized variants) and inference config (temp/decoding, kv cache settings, quantization).
[02:05] Maya: We're also worried about running vLLM/TGI artifacts. We have some finetunes packaged for TGI and some inference-as-a-service glue that expects the TGI API.
[02:13] Samir: That's a common pattern. Redwood's runtime supports TGI-compatible endpoints and we have a migration layer for vLLM artifacts in many cases. There's occasionally small work required to adapt tokenizers or model config. Jia can go into specifics.
[02:25] Jia: Right - practically we do two things: 1) run your eval set against candidate models on Redwood Dedicated and compare metrics; 2) if you have TGI artifacts, we can try a conversion/import and run them in a sandbox. For vLLM workloads, we can often replicate the same batching/kv-cache behavior but need to tune kernel choices.
[02:44] Liam: Any examples of customers who've moved from OpenAI and kept their eval pass rates?
[02:49] Jia: Yes - e.g., a search-vertical customer migrated and kept >95% of their production eval pass rate after tweaking temp/top_p and moving to a slightly larger open model. Another kept parity by enabling per-request prefix caching. We'll share case notes.
[03:02] Samir: Also note that some teams choose a staged approach: duplicate traffic to Dedicated for A/B, compare outputs and latency, then flip once stable. That helps with regression detection.
[03:12] Maya: Makes sense. On security - we need SOC 2, SSO via SAML, KMS integration for keys, and audit logs. Also some data residency constraints - EU-only for certain customer data.
[03:23] Oliver (Redwood CSM): We support SOC 2, SSO with SAML/Okta, and customer-managed KMS/HSM options for Private. For Dedicated we provide per-customer isolation; for Private we can do VPC/on-prem with customer-controlled keys.
[03:36] Priya: For Dedicated, is the control plane hosted by Redwood? How about network egress? We need to ensure traffic doesn't traverse unknown regions for EU data.
[03:45] Jia: Dedicated typically uses a shared control plane but data plane in the dedicated GPU pool as provisioned; for EU residency we can provision capacity in a regional cloud and ensure egress stays in-region. For highly regulated use-cases, Private (VPC or on-prem) is the path. We'll send the infra whitepaper.
[03:59] Maya: Great. Cost: our CFO wants to see delta vs OpenAI. We pay per-token now but it's creeping up. What's the typical unit cost delta for Dedicated?
[04:09] Samir: It depends on utilization and model. Rough ballpark: at your volumes Dedicated often reduces per-token unit cost materially - sometimes 2-5x cheaper at steady-state because you amortize GPU costs. But upfront committed capacity and sustained utilization matter. We'll put numbers in the sizing/pricing sheet.
[04:24] Liam: Another operational question: we run streaming for chat. How does Redwood handle prefix caching and continuous batching without increasing latency?
[04:33] Jia: Our runtime supports continuous batching with latency-aware policies, and prefix/KV caching to reduce compute on repeated prompts. For streaming we maintain low tail latency by prioritizing small batches for critical flows. The tradeoff is you might give up some batching efficiency to meet p95 latencies.
[04:51] Maya: Could you run a quick back-of-napkin on the machines - like what GPU types we need to hit 400 qps at 1.2k tokens, p95 150ms?
[05:00] Jia: Off the cuff, 400 qps at that token size is fairly heavy. We'll need a pool of high-memory A100s or H100-equivalents with optimized kernels; but exact sizing depends on model (size) and quantization. For example, if you can move to a quantized 8-bit variant, throughput improves a lot. We'll get precise numbers after we run a synthetic benchmark with your prompts.
[05:18] Priya: We do have GPU limits in our cloud tenant; we might prefer Redwood-hosted Dedicated rather than on-prem. But network egress constraints still apply.
[05:26] Samir: Totally - part of the pilot will validate performance in your region and with your network topology. We'll do a test run either from Redwood in-region infra or within your VPC if you go Private.
[05:38] Noah: About logs and PII - can we redact or avoid storing user-level inputs? We have strict privacy rules.
[05:46] Oliver: We support configurable logging and can disable persistent request storage for Dedicated; for Private you control logs entirely. We also offer field-level redaction and integrations with SIEM. We'll share docs.
[05:59] Liam: Ok, on the compatibility side - our fine-tunes are in TGI format with custom tokenizers. How painful is importing them?
[06:06] Jia: Usually it's straightforward if the tokenizer metadata is included. If it's custom, we may need to run a short conversion. Typical path: import artifact -> run smoke tests -> run eval set. Could be a few days depending on complexity.
[06:18] Maya: We'd want to run our eval set and check for regressions. I'd like to schedule that bench and have Redwood run an apples-to-apples with our current OpenAI config.
[06:26] Samir: Absolutely. Jia will run the benchmark and we'll do traffic duplication if you want. We'll need your eval set and a few representative production requests.
[06:34] Priya: Network wise, we need to know what ports and peering steps you require if we go Private. Also any IP allowlist for Dedicated control plane calls.
[06:42] Jia: We'll provide a network runbook with IP ranges, ports, and peering instructions. For Dedicated, control plane calls can be locked down; for Private we can avoid control plane network egress if you choose on-prem.
[06:53] Liam: Quick tangent - do you have an autoscaler that reacts to burst traffic? Our load can spike 3x during marketing pushes.
[07:00] Jia: Dedicated pools support configurable autoscaling and burst buffers; you can define policies for guaranteed baseline and temporary burst capacity. Pricing varies for burst usage.
[07:09] Maya: Good. Anyone on security side asking about pen tests and certifications? We require vendor pen test reports and SOC documents before procurement.
[07:17] Oliver: We'll share SOC 2 attestations and an available pen test summary; for in-depth audits we have an enterprise security pack. I'll include that in the security packet.
[07:27] Samir: Ok quick check - timeline: are you evaluating this for a Q2 pilot?
[07:33] Maya: Yes, we want a pilot in Q2, production by late Q3 if results are good. Budget approved for a pilot.
[07:40] Samir: Great. We'll prioritize the benchmark. Jia, can you summarize the technical next steps?
[07:45] Jia: Sure - 1) Ardent shares eval set + sample prompts; 2) Redwood runs evals on candidate models and your TGI artifacts; 3) we run a latency/throughput benchmark with synthetic traffic and then optionally duplicate prod traffic; 4) we share tuning recommendations and a sizing/pricing sheet. I'll schedule the deep dive.
[08:06] Maya: Sounds good. A couple of small asks: can Redwood sign our DPPA addendum? And can we get a non-disclosure for the finetune artifacts?
[08:16] Samir: Yes we have standard DPAs/DPPA addenda and an NDA. I'll have legal loop in if needed; we'll send the contract templates.
[08:24] Liam: For the benchmark, can you mimic streaming behavior and token-by-token latency? Our main pain is tail latency on long chats.
[08:31] Jia: We'll include streaming scenarios and measure token-by-token tail latency. We'll report p50/p90/p95 and also per-request token throughput.
[08:40] Noah: If we find a small regression in generation quality, is there an option to fall back to OpenAI for certain flows?
[08:46] Samir: Yes - Redwood routing supports policy-based fallbacks to a hosted provider. Many customers run a hybrid where low-latency or high-quality flows are routed differently.
[08:56] Priya: One more on encryption - KMS integration: do you offer customer-managed keys for Dedicated or only for Private?
[09:03] Oliver: For Dedicated we offer KMS integration for data at rest keys in many configurations; for full customer-managed HSM, Private is the option. We'll note exact supported KMS providers in the security packet.
[09:16] Maya: Ok, that covers most of it. Any blockers from you?
[09:20] Samir: No blockers. We'll get you a pricing/sizing sheet and security docs. Jia will schedule the tech deep dive and benchmark.
[09:28] Liam: Quick nit - do you support inference caching for personalized prefixes? We rely on prefix caching heavily.
[09:33] Jia: Yes, we support prefix/KV caching and per-customer cache policies. We'll include cache hit rates expected in the benchmark.
[09:43] Maya: Perfect. Let's recap next steps.
[09:46] Samir: Recap - Samir to send pricing & sizing by 2026-03-06; Jia to schedule tech deep dive and run benchmarks by 2026-03-09; Ardent to share eval set and finetune artifacts by 2026-03-05; Redwood to send security pack and DPA templates.
[10:02] Maya: Great, thanks. We'll look out for the invite and docs.
[10:06] Samir: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email.
[10:10] (call ends)

Notes about transcription: occasional speaker overlaps noted; some proper nouns may be mis-transcribed (TGI/TJ? vLLM sometimes becomes 'vee-l m'). We kept natural hesitations and brief crosstalk to preserve realism.
